prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on your case details, priorities, and personality fit. I can’t single out one definitive winner, but I can help you find the best lawyer for your Dallas truck-accident claim and tell you exactly how to evaluate candidates.

What matters most
- Proven truck-accident experience (commercial trucking cases, FMCSA/regulatory knowledge, dealing with trucking companies and their insurers).  
- Trial experience and resources (these cases often require expensive experts—accident reconstruction, trucking operations, electronic logging device/black box analysis).  
- Track record of strong verdicts/settlements in truck cases.  
- Clear contingency-fee agreement and transparent costs.  
- Good communication, responsiveness, and client references.  
- Local knowledge of Dallas courts and judges.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar “Find a Lawyer” (to verify license and discipline history).  
- Super Lawyers and Martindale-Hubbell (peer reviews).  
- Avvo and Google/Yelp for client reviews (read specifics, not just scores).  
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association or National Trial Lawyers (lists of top plaintiffs’ attorneys).  
- Local Dallas law firms that handle trucking collisions—look for firms advertising trucking-specific teams.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
1. How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
2. Do you handle only plaintiffs’ cases or also defense? (Prefer plaintiffs-only for conflicts and focus.)  
3. What similar verdicts/settlements have you obtained? Can you share redacted examples?  
4. What experts will you use (accident reconstruction, trucking operations, medical)? Who are they?  
5. How will you charge (contingency %, expenses advanced or deducted)?  
6. Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)? Who will I contact?  
7. Do you anticipate need for hiring experts, obtaining driver logs, ELD data, or pursuing punitive damages?  
8. What is your strategy for my case and an estimated timeline?  
9. Are there any conflicts of interest?  
10. Can you provide client references?

Documents to bring to the consultation
- Police/accident report, photos/video, medical records, medical bills, wage records, insurance info, contact info for witnesses, truck company name/DOT number, any correspondence from insurers.

Practical tips and red flags
- Act quickly: Texas statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the accident date (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003).  
- Red flags: attorney promises a specific result, asks for large upfront fees, poor communication, no willingness to try the case in court, no trucking-specific experience.  
- Good sign: lawyer immediately discusses obtaining driver logs, ELD/black box data, maintenance and inspection records, and FMCSA violations.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft a short script/email to contact several Dallas attorneys.  
- Recommend how to compare final offers.  
- Look up top-rated Dallas plaintiff firms if you give your ZIP code or permission to recommend a short list (I can’t browse in real time, but I can suggest well-known sources and search terms).

Would you like a short template you can use to contact 4–6 lawyers for initial consultations? Or provide your ZIP/neighborhood and I’ll help narrow options and the best ways to reach them.
